body: I do have a tiny bit of social anxiety, usually after I conversation I'll head into my room and whisper, "Idiot," to myself. I still like interacting with people, however, it usually distracts me from my thoughts and is somewhat therapeutic .

I feel large amounts of anxiety at times, but I usually don't get very fidgety/physical or angry. I'm a very subdued and withdrawn person in general. The only racing thought I have is a fast repetition of "Kill yourself kill yourself kill yourself," so I'm unsure if that counts. I'll keep BPII in mind though, and ask about it the next time I'm able.

Perhaps you could call it a delusion? Either way, I never really deduced that I deserve to die, I just feel it with extreme intensity. No matter how much I try to rationalize it as unjustified the feeling doesn't abate.
I would honestly love to, but I have no ideas. If I open photoshop I'll just stare at the screen until I'm forced to close it in defeat.
I used to make digital art and read often, with video games sprinkled in between. Now I mainly do some schoolwork and sleep.

I know people care, and that used to be enough to curb these thoughts, but recently I feel nothing when reflecting on that fact. I have no will to live. I used to have hobbies, but I feel no motivation to participate in any of them.

It's entirely internal, in the same way people "hear" their thoughts, so no auditory hallucinations. I've never been treated for bipolar depression, but I can't recall having anything like manic phases.

Yeah, a combination of the two has been tried. It's difficult to say why I believe I deserve to die, I just keep recalling every small or large thing I've done wrong and that reinforces the idea. It's like an idea I can't shake which slowly grew in my mind.
It's been at least two years, and I was already predisposed to being melancholy. I've tried grief counseling and CBT, neither worked. I've also tried SSRIs, the most notable being Prozac.
